content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Variable-Length Arguments** as part of **Functions and Parameters**. Apply variable-length arguments by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—The vararg Modifier, Passing Arrays with the Spread Operator, Designing Variable-Argument APIs—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.

items.title: The vararg Modifier
items.text: The vararg Modifier is one part of variable-length arguments. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Passing Arrays with the Spread Operator
items.text: Passing Arrays with the Spread Operator is best learned by tracing a small collection before and after the operation. Check ordering, duplicate handling, empty inputs, and whether the API returns a new value or mutates a mutable receiver.

items.title: Designing Variable-Argument APIs
items.text: Designing Variable-Argument APIs crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.
